prompt: More and more people I know say they won't have kids because of climate change, AI risk, or because the money would do more good elsewhere. I'm about to start a family myself, and I don't find the usual 'it's natural, just have kids' response convincing as an answer to that. Write a personal essay that takes these social-movement arguments against having children seriously and tries to work out what's really underneath them.
Is teaching kids to code actually worth it if programming keeps getting more abstracted and AI-assisted? What's the real point?

Write an essay on how ideologies in tech, effective altruism being the clearest case, turn into working machinery that moves money and people toward real outcomes. What are the parts of that machinery, how does it compare to the big philanthropic foundations of the 20th century, and should we want more of these things or fewer? Assume a reader who knows tech but isn't an EA.
Effective altruists talk as if there's one objectively best way to give money away. Is that a reasonable way to think about philanthropy?
Federal R&D spending dwarfs anything tech billionaires put into science. So how do private science funders expect to make a difference?

Everyone is excited about the 'creator economy' and the new tools that let people make a living publishing online. I have mixed feelings about it. Write a reflective essay on what it actually means to be a 'creator' and whether the constant pressure to keep producing serves culture or just fills it up.
I spend most of my days reading. How do I tell whether I'm doing research or just entertaining myself?
